snippet.description:
Switzerland did not invent chocolate — but it perfected it.

Chocolate originally came from the Americas, where cacao was used long before it became popular in Europe. For centuries, chocolate was mostly a bitter drink enjoyed by the rich. But in the 1800s, Switzerland changed chocolate history forever.

Daniel Peter created milk chocolate by mixing chocolate with powdered milk, while Rodolphe Lindt invented a machine that made chocolate silky smooth. With Alpine milk, skilled makers, Swiss precision, and the beauty of the Swiss Alps, Switzerland became famous for chocolate around the world.

This short documentary by StateOrigins tells the story of how Switzerland became the chocolate capital of the world, how milk chocolate changed everything, and why Swiss chocolate still rules today.
